newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shop lobby opposes further liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: German shop lobby opposes further liberalisation.

text.p: The German retail lobby on Tuesday opposed the scrapping of restrictions on shop opening hours proposed in a monopoly commission report, saying the recent loosening of 40-year-old limits on closing times was enough.

Several retail groups said they also rejected commission recommendations to scrap a law preventing discounting, saying that full liberalisation would kill off local shops and benefit big store chains.
"There is no need...to strengthen price competition in the German retail sector through cut-throat discounting," Holger Wenzel, of the German Retailers Association (HDE), said in a statement.
The monopoly commission was reporting its findings to Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt, who has been a champion of freeing up Germany's antiquated shop opening laws.
Shop hours were extended by 1-1/2 hours to eight p.m. on weekdays from November 1, while stores can stay open two hours later on Saturdays until four p.m.

Small and medium-sized German retailers had been bitterly opposed to the changes in store hours, but ultimately accepted them and are now looking to boost Christmas sales after four years of stagnation.
